timing_rule: Latest eligible year per source within 3 years; dated fieldwork must end before the decision, otherwise an earlier calendar year is required. Retain all eligible question variants in that year.

general_access.support_definition: Source-specific general abortion preferences: ANES original categories, GSS any-reason legality, PRRI legal all/most. These are contextual and not interchangeable.

retain_roe.support_definition: Retain Roe: code 2 supports retention, code 1 opposes retention.

cases.name: Roe v. Wade

components.issue: Protection against a life-saving-only abortion ban
components.decision: Invalidated the Texas prohibition and recognized constitutional protection subject to pregnancy-stage limits.
components.scope: Protection was not unlimited at every pregnancy stage.
components.survey_fit: General permission categories supply context; they do not ask about constitutional protection or the stage-dependent framework.

observations.wording:
(1972,1976: Still on the subject of women’s rights,)
           There has been some discussion about abortion during recent years.
           Which one of the opinions on this page (1972: card) best agrees with
           your view? You can just tell me the number of the opinion you choose.
observations.denominator: Positive-weight coded answers 1–4 and DK/other (9); code 0 combines missing/not-administered and is excluded. Not a full-sample denominator.
observations.category_definition:
1. Abortion should never be permitted.
           2. Abortion should be permitted only if the life and health of the woman is
           in danger.
           3. Abortion should be permitted if, due to personal reasons, the woman would
           have diﬃculty in caring for the child.
           4. Abortion should never be forbidden, since one should not require a woman
           to have a child she doesn’t want.
           9. DK; other

response_distribution.label: Only danger to life and health

cases.interpretation_limit: Historical holding, later overruled. Broad permission is not approval of the full Roe framework.

cases.name: Harris v. McRae

components.issue: Public financing of medically necessary abortions
components.decision: Upheld Hyde funding restrictions; Medicaid participation did not require states to fund abortions excluded from federal reimbursement.
components.scope: Public subsidy obligations, distinct from permission to obtain an abortion.
components.locator: Opinion Parts II and III; syllabus holdings 1 and 2.
components.survey_fit: No funding-specific observation is included. General legality and abortion in cases of poverty do not measure public-financing preferences.

cases.interpretation_limit: Direct denotes the policy a suitable question would need to address; none is matched. No funding agreement is inferred.

cases.name: Planned Parenthood v. Casey

components.decision: Retained Roe’s essential protection while replacing its trimester framework with the undue-burden standard.
components.scope: Core protection retained; regulatory doctrine changed.
components.locator: Joint opinion Parts I and IV.
components.survey_fit: General abortion preferences are context, not a referendum on this legal standard.

observations.wording:
ALL YEARS EXCEPT 2000 TELEPHONE:
           There has been some discussion about abortion during recent years.
           (RESPONDENT BOOKLET) Which one of the opinions on this page best agrees
           with your view? You can just tell me the number of the opinion you
           choose.
           2000 TELEPHONE:
           I am going to read you a short list of opinions. Please tell me which


            one of the opinions best agrees with your view. You can just tell me the
            number of the opinion you choose.
observations.denominator: Positive-weight coded answers 1–4 and DK/other (9); code 0 combines missing/not-administered and is excluded. Not a full-sample denominator.
observations.category_definition:
1. By law, abortion should never be permitted.
            2. The law should permit abortion only in case of rape, incest, or when the
            woman’s life is in danger.
            3. The law should permit abortion for reasons other than rape, incest, or
            danger to the woman’s life, but only after the need for the abortion has
            been clearly established.
            4. By law, a woman should always be able to obtain an abortion as a matter of
            personal choice.
            9. DK; other

response_distribution.label: Only rape, incest, or danger to life
Other reasons if need clearly established

components.decision: Invalidated Texas admitting-privileges and surgical-center requirements.
components.scope: Removed the challenged provider barriers, not all abortion regulation.
components.locator: Breyer opinion introduction and Parts IV–V.
components.survey_fit: General legality supplies context only; no selected question specifically measures either provider requirement.

cases.name: Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization

components.decision: Removed federal constitutional abortion protection by overruling Roe and Casey.
components.scope: Removal of federal protection, not enactment of a nationwide abortion ban.
components.survey_fit: Asks about overturning Roe, matching the overruling component. Fieldwork was largely after the draft leak but before the judgment.

observations.wording_note: Paraphrased question summary; original wording and context are in the report. Form A half sample; fieldwork largely followed the draft-opinion leak.
observations.denominator: Published full item response distribution, including uncertainty; percentages retained as reported.
observations.survey_fit: Asks about overturning Roe, matching the overruling component. Fieldwork was largely after the draft leak but before the judgment.

observations.wording: As you may know, the 1973 Supreme Court Case Roe v. Wade established a woman's constitutional right to have an abortion. Would you like to see the Supreme Court overturn its Roe v. Wade decision, or not?
observations.denominator: All positive-weight November-wave respondents, including not sure and skipped; no yes/no-only renormalization.
observations.orientation: Support = retain Roe; oppose = overturn Roe. Not general abortion legality.

limitations: Explicit source-based legal coding is an input, not an automated legal classifier.
Contextual matches do not measure approval of the specific holding.
Mixed and unresolved components retain their labels; no scalar direction is inferred.
No pooling, confidence intervals, causal claims, or prediction.
